'''Yuri Ivanovich Manin''' ({{langx|ru|link=no|Ю́рий Ива́нович Ма́нин}}) (16 February 1937 – 7 January 2023) was a Russian mathematician, known for work in [[algebraic geometry]] and [[diophantine geometry]], and many expository works ranging from [[mathematical logic]] to [[theoretical physics]].

== Life and career ==
Manin was born on 16 February 1937 in [[Simferopol]], Crimean ASSR<!-- DO NOT LINK, see [[MOS:GEOLINK]] for further guidance -->, Soviet Union<!-- DO NOT LINK, see [[MOS:GEOLINK]] for further guidance -->.<ref name="mpim-death"/>

He received a doctorate in 1960 at the [[Steklov Mathematics Institute]] as a student of [[Igor Shafarevich]]. He became a professor at the [[Max-Planck-Institut für Mathematik]] in [[Bonn]], where he was director from 1992 to 2005 and then director emeritus.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/node/99|title=Yuri Manin {{!}} Max Planck Institute for Mathematics|website=www.mpim-bonn.mpg.de|language=en|access-date=6 August 2018}}</ref><ref name="mpim-death"/> He was also a Trustee Chair Professor at [[Northwestern University]] from 2002 to 2011.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Yuri Manin – Northwestern University |url=https://apps.math.northwestern.edu/yuri_manin/ |access-date=20 May 2024 |website=math.northwestern.edu |language=en}}</ref>

He had over the years more than 50 doctoral students, including [[Vladimir Berkovich]], [[Mariusz Wodzicki]], [[Alexander Beilinson]], [[Ivan Cherednik]], [[Alexei Skorobogatov]], [[Vladimir Drinfeld]], [[Mikhail Kapranov]], [[Vyacheslav Shokurov]], [[Ralph Kaufmann]],  [[Victor Kolyvagin]], [[Alexander L. Rosenberg]], [[Alexander A. Voronov]], and [[Hà Huy Khoái]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy |id=44207}}</ref>

Manin died on 7 January 2023 in Bonn.<ref name="mpim-death">{{cite web |title=Max Planck Institute for Mathematics in Bonn Mourns Death of Yuri Manin |url=https://www.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/node/11864 |website=[[Max Planck Institute for Mathematics]] |date=8 January 2023 |access-date=8 January 2023}}</ref>

== Research ==
Manin's early work included papers on the arithmetic and [[formal group]]s of [[abelian varieties]], the [[Mordell conjecture]] in the [[global function field|function field]] case, and [[algebraic differential equation]]s. The [[Gauss–Manin connection]] is a basic ingredient of the study of [[cohomology]] in families of [[algebraic varieties]].<ref>{{Citation | last1=Manin | first1=Ju. I. | author-link=Yuri Manin| title=Algebraic curves over fields with differentiation | url=http://mi.mathnet.ru/eng/izv/v22/i6/p737 | language=Russian | mr=0103889 | year=1958 | journal=Izvestiya Akademii Nauk SSSR. Seriya Matematicheskaya | volume=22 | pages=737–756}} English translation in {{Citation | last1=Manin | first1=Ju. I. | title=American Mathematical Society translations: 22 papers on algebra, number theory and differential geometry | year=1964| url=https://books.google.com/books?id=fZ7ms3db_cMC | publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]] | location=Providence, R.I. | isbn=978-0-8218-1737-7 | mr=0103889 | volume=37 | chapter=Algebraic curves over fields with differentiation | pages=59–78}} English translation published by the AMS in 1964.</ref><ref>{{eom|title=Gauss-Manin connection}}</ref>

He developed the [[Manin obstruction]], indicating the role of the [[Brauer group]] in accounting for obstructions to the [[Hasse principle]] via [[Grothendieck]]'s theory of global [[Azumaya algebra]]s, setting off a generation of further work.<ref>{{cite book | author=Serge Lang | authorlink=Serge Lang | title=Survey of Diophantine geometry | publisher=[[Springer-Verlag]] | year=1997 | isbn=978-3-540-61223-0 | zbl=0869.11051 | pages=250–258 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | author=Alexei N. Skorobogatov | title=Beyond the Manin obstruction | journal=[[Inventiones Mathematicae]] | others=Appendix A by S. Siksek: 4-descent | volume=135 | issue=2 | pages=399–424 | year=1999 | doi=10.1007/s002220050291 | zbl=0951.14013 | arxiv=alg-geom/9711006 | bibcode=1999InMat.135..399S | s2cid=14285244 }}</ref>

Manin pioneered the field of [[arithmetic topology]] (along with [[John Tate (mathematician)|John Tate]], [[David Mumford]], [[Michael Artin]], and [[Barry Mazur]]).<ref>{{cite book |last=Morishita |first=Masanori |year=2012 |chapter=Introduction |title=Knots and Primes |series=Universitext |pages=1–7 |publisher=[[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer]] |location=London |doi=10.1007/978-1-4471-2158-9_1|isbn=978-1-4471-2157-2 }}</ref> He also formulated the [[Manin conjecture]], which predicts the asymptotic behaviour of the number of rational points of bounded height on algebraic varieties.<ref>
{{cite journal
  | last1=Franke | first1 = J. | last2 = Manin | first2 = Y. I. | author2-link = Yuri I. Manin | last3 = Tschinkel | first3 = Y.
  | title = Rational points of bounded height on Fano varieties
  | journal = [[Inventiones Mathematicae]]
  | volume = 95
  | year = 1989
  | issue = 2
  | pages = 421–435
  | mr = 974910
  | zbl = 0674.14012 | doi=10.1007/bf01393904| bibcode = 1989InMat..95..421F | s2cid = 121044839 }}
</ref>

In mathematical physics, Manin wrote on [[Yang–Mills theory]], [[quantum information]], and [[mirror symmetry (string theory)|mirror symmetry]].<ref>{{cite journal |first1=Michael |last1=Atiyah |authorlink=Michael Atiyah |first2=Vladimir |last2=Drinfeld |authorlink2=Vladimir Drinfeld |first3=Nigel |last3=Hitchin |authorlink3=Nigel Hitchin |first4=Yuri |last4=Manin |title=Construction of instantons |journal=[[Physics Letters A]] |volume=65 |year=1978 |issue=3 |pages=185–187|doi=10.1016/0375-9601(78)90141-X |bibcode=1978PhLA...65..185A }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Devchand |first1=Chandrashekar |last2=Ogievetsky |first2=Victor I. |chapter=Integrability of N=3 super Yang-Mills equations |title=Topics in statistical and theoretical physics |pages=51–58 |series=Amer. Math. Soc. Transl. Ser. 2 |volume=177 |publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]] |location=Providence, RI |year=1996}}</ref> He was one of the first to propose the idea of a [[quantum computer]] in [[Timeline of quantum computing|1980]] with his book ''Computable and Uncomputable''.<ref name="manin1980vychislimoe">{{cite book| author=Manin, Yu. I.| title=Vychislimoe i nevychislimoe|trans-title=Computable and Noncomputable| year=1980| publisher=Sov.Radio| url=http://publ.lib.ru/ARCHIVES/M/MANIN_Yuriy_Ivanovich/_Manin_Yu.I..zip| pages=13–15| language=ru| access-date=4 March 2013| url-status=dead| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130510173823/http://publ.lib.ru/ARCHIVES/M/MANIN_Yuriy_Ivanovich/Manin_Yu.I._Vychislimoe_i_nevychislimoe.%281980%29.%5Bdjv%5D.zip| archive-date=10 May 2013}}</ref>

He wrote a book on [[cubic surface]]s and [[cubic form]]s, showing how to apply both classical and contemporary methods of algebraic geometry, as well as [[nonassociative algebra]].<ref>{{cite book | last=Manin | first=I͡U. I. | title=Cubic Forms: Algebra, Geometry, Arithmetic | publisher=North Holland | publication-place=Amsterdam; New York : New York, NY, U.S.A | date=1986 | url= https://www.sciencedirect.com/bookseries/north-holland-mathematical-library/vol/4 | isbn=978-0-444-87823-6 }}</ref>

== Awards ==
He was awarded the [[Brouwer Medal]] in 1987, the first [[Nemmers Prize in Mathematics]] in 1994, the [[Schock Prize]] of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]] in 1999, the [[Cantor Medal]] of the [[German Mathematical Society]] in 2002, the [[King Faisal International Prize]] in 2002, and the [[Bolyai Prize]] of the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]] in 2010.<ref name="mpim-death"/>

In 1990, he became a foreign member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/foreign-members/4514 |title=Y.I. Manin |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |access-date=19 July 2015 |archive-date=8 August 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200808001426/https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/foreign-members/4514 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was a member of eight other academies of science and was also an honorary member of the [[London Mathematical Society]].<ref name="mpim-death"/>
